reels.title: A day on Venus is longer than its year
reels.hook: One spin of Venus takes longer than its whole trip around the Sun.
reels.caption:
A day on Venus is longer than its year. 🪐

Venus turns so slowly that one spin on its axis takes about 243 Earth days. One trip around the Sun takes only about 225.

And it spins backwards. If you could see through its thick clouds, you'd watch the Sun rise in the west and set in the east.

Which fact got you: the day or the sunrise? 👇

Source: NASA Science, Venus facts.
reels.alt_text: A 3D-animated Venus with swirling pale-yellow clouds turns slowly in space, then is shown orbiting a glowing Sun before the Sun rises over its edge. Bold captions read "1 day > 1 year?", "1 spin = 243 days", "1 orbit = 225 days" and "Sunrise: west".

reels.title: Saturn would float in water
reels.hook: Saturn is nine times wider than Earth, yet on average it's less dense than water.
reels.caption:
Saturn could float in a bathtub. 🪐🛁

It's about 9 times wider than Earth, but it's mostly hydrogen and helium, so its average density is less than water's.

That makes it the only planet in our solar system that would float, if you could find a tub big enough.

Which would you rather see: Saturn in a bathtub or Saturn up close? 👇

Source: NASA Science, Saturn facts.
reels.alt_text: A 3D-animated Saturn with golden bands and wide rings floats on a calm sea, is compared in size with a small blue Earth, then bobs in the water before the camera pulls back to reveal a giant bathtub. Bold captions read "Could Saturn float?", "9× wider than Earth", "Less dense than water" and "The only planet that floats".
